title: SDK Report
description:
Per-platform evidence that a build's platform SDK integration works: which SDK features each target platform requires, and whether each is working on that platform.

prototype-report.integration_status says whether the SDK works in aggregate; this says which platform and which feature, because a portal can reject what another portal accepted. Every `working` claim should name how it was observed.

Since 1.1.0 it can also say how the integration was made: the SDK revision the game carries and the calls its `Platform` interface offers, which adapter each platform resolves to, which gameplay hooks call into it, what a platform cannot do and what the game does instead, and what the integration's own tests found. All of that is optional, so a 1.0.0 report still validates. A feature observed only against SDK mocks says so in `observed_by`: it is evidence that the game is wired, never that a portal accepted the build.

commit_sha.description: The commit the report is about: the sdk step's own integration commit when it made one, else the HEAD it verified.

base_commit_sha.description: Since 1.2.0. The commit the integration was made on: the prototype-report's build_ref.commit_sha. Equal to commit_sha when the step committed nothing. Absent in older reports, which are read as base == commit_sha.

sdk_commits.description: Since 1.2.0. The commits the sdk step made between base_commit_sha and commit_sha, oldest first, each carrying a `Wgf-Sdk-Key: <run>:<step>:<visit>` trailer. Empty when it committed nothing. git log base..commit must list exactly these.

sdk.description: The template's platform SDK as found in the game repository. Revisions differ in which adapters and calls they have, so an integration is checked against this, not against a copy.

adapter.description: What the SDK's registry constructs for this platform id. `substituted`: the portal publishes no SDK, and builds for it run on `adapter_id` by explicit configuration. `missing`: no adapter, and a build for this platform fails at boot.

portal_sdk.description: The portal SDK script the adapter loads, where it names one.

feature.description: e.g. init, loading-progress, rewarded, interstitial, banner, cloud-save, analytics

status.description: unsupported: the design needs it, but the platform, its adapter or the SDK's API does not offer it; `fallback` says what the game does instead.

required_by.description: What in the design needs this feature.

hooks.description: The gameplay hooks that carry the feature, as named in integration.game_hooks.

fallback.description: What the game does when the feature is unsupported here, or unavailable at runtime.

integration.description: What the integration changed in the game repository, and the evidence that it works.

repository_state.description: Whether build_ref.commit_sha already contains the integration. `uncommitted-changes`: the working tree is ahead of it.

placements.description: Each game-design monetization placement and the gameplay moment it was attached to. `moment` is absent where the trigger matched none.
